sam: Quick weekend run on novaX-8b (int4) vs flux-8b (fp16). Cost per 1k tokens: fp16 ~$0.27 -> int4 ~$0.08. But we see recall/precision drop on long doc QA slices and some hallucination uptick.

jia: Can you paste the slice metrics and a tiny example? baseline numbers?

sam: Baseline: flux-8b fp16. Snapshot: precision@5 0.71 -> 0.63 (doc-qa), exact-match down 4.5%. Latency p95 ~unchanged. Repro command: `./scripts/quant_eval.sh --model novaX --q int4 --slices doc-qa,short-chat`

miguel: Did you check KV-cache hit rates? int4 sometimes nudges probability mass and the beam picks shorter sequences.

sam: KV hits stable in logs. Samples show shorter answers and more confident wrong tokens on factual prompts. Example generation (short): 
`Q: Who founded Redwood Inference?
A (fp16): "Founded by a team including ..."
A (int4): "Company was started by Redwood, based in SF."`

tara: From product POV: GTN would accept int4 for summarization but not for customer-facing chat if hallucination increases. What's ops recommendation?

jia: Recommend we require a minimal scorecard for rollout:
- unit_cost_delta (pct)
- precision@k delta
- recall delta
- hallucination_rate (absolute ppm)
- latency tail (p95/p99)
- number of regressed prompts in critical set
If any metric regresses beyond thresholds (e.g., precision drop > 5% or hallucination +3% abs) we holdback.

miguel: Operationally I suggest hybrid routing canary: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automatic fallback to fp16 on slices where delta_precision < -0.05. Route rules: token_length > 1024 OR slice==doc-qa OR header x-intent in ["legal","billing","support"].

sam: Ran a tiny canary with header-based routing (500 sessions): product signals mixed but not catastrophic. Will do a 10k blind eval next.

tara: For GTN guidance: pick a 10k sample split by top intents + longform content, include adversarial prompts. I'll own constructing that set. @jia can you provide the scorecard template?

sam: Pasting quick scorecard snippet: 
```
slice,baseline_prec5,quant_prec5,delta_prec5,baseline_cost_per1k,quant_cost_per1k
doc-qa,0.71,0.63,-0.08,0.27,0.08
short-chat,0.85,0.83,-0.02,0.27,0.08
summary,0.79,0.78,-0.01,0.27,0.08
```

miguel: Routing-service rule to add: `if (slice == \"doc-qa\" && model.q == \"int4\" && delta_prec5 < -0.05) { route = fp16 }` — I'll file a change.

tara: Also need product cost calc to show incremental cost if we do hybrid routing. Sam, can you compute 25% fp16 / 75% int4 blended cost?

sam: Quick calc: blended cost per 1k = 0.75*0.08 + 0.25*0.27 = 0.1275 ~ $0.13 (≈1.6x cheaper than 100% fp16). Will produce per-10k-query numbers once I have average tokens/session.

jia: Draft GTN recommendation outline: default int4 for short queries and summaries, int4 for batch/async non-critical traffic, route to fp16 for doc-qa / high-importance intents, require holdback if hallucination delta > 3% absolute or precision@5 drop > 5%.

tara: I'll write the rollout note and GTN checklist (canary sizes, guardrail metrics, rollback steps). Thanks all :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created canary routing rule id=7789 in routing-service (details link: https://k.rw/deploy/7789)

sam: Next steps I own: 1) finalize scorecard template, 2) run 10k blind eval with adversarial prompts, 3) implement hybrid routing rule + canary, 4) handoff GTN note for product signoff.

If anyone wants the raw csv or logs I can drop into the eng-ml drive.
